meta.description: Mean player positions per role conditioned on the ball cell and possession (DFL)
meta.source: DFL/Sportec open data: Bassek, M., Rein, R., Weber, H., Memmert, D. (2025). An integrated dataset of spatiotemporal and event data in elite soccer. Scientific Data 12:195. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-04505-y. Licence: CC-BY 4.0. Aggregate statistics only; no raw, frame-level or person-level data.
meta.licence: CC-BY 4.0 (data); these aggregates are derived statistics with attribution

config.xg_angle_slope_source: Soccermatics angle-only logistic fit, logit(xG) = -3.52 + 2.84 * theta, on 8,451 shots of the 2017/18 Premier League in the open Wyscout data (Pappalardo et al. 2019, Scientific Data 6:236, doi:10.1038/s41597-019-0247-7, CC BY 4.0)

conventions.coordinates: metres, centre origin, team-attacking direction: the team attacks +x, left is +y; pitch 105 x 68 m
conventions.validity: valid samples only (valid_kinematics = true); estimated gap samples never count for speed, peaks or per-90 values
conventions.per90: normalised on measured (valid) time of each player-match (team decision 2026-10-24); see coverage
conventions.ball: ball status and possession are the provider's (never derived from a stationary ball)

notes: Samples: player valid, ball live and valid, a team in possession (provider); 13,232,218 samples before mirror pooling.
Coordinates: the player's team attacks +x, left is +y (centre origin, metres, scaled to 105 x 68 m). The ball cell uses the same coordinates.
Grids are indexed [ix][iy]: ix over x_edges (12 bins, own goal -> opponent goal), iy over y_edges (8 bins, right touchline y = -34 -> left touchline y = +34).

Mirror pooling: right-side roles are mirrored (y -> -y) into their left partner (RB -> LB, RCB -> LCB, RWB -> LWB, RDM -> LDM, RCM -> LCM, RM -> LM, RW -> LW, RS -> LS) and the right map is the mirror of the pooled left map; central roles (GK, CB, CDM, CM, CAM, ST) are pooled with their own mirror, so their maps are symmetric. count includes the mirrored copies.

Fallback (cells with count < 50): the role's mean position in that possession state (baseline) plus the role group's mean shift for that ball cell (fallback.<GROUP>: displacement from each role's own baseline, left orientation, pooled over the group's roles). If the group cell is also below the threshold, the baseline is used. source tells which: 'role', 'group' or 'baseline'. sd_x/sd_y of fallback cells are the group's (or the role's overall) spread.
CM has no DFL samples (DFL has no plain central-midfield code; HL/HR map to LCM/RCM): its baseline is the CM group's mean x with y = 0 and every cell comes from the group or the baseline.
